```{r setup, include = FALSE}
## The notebook runs from the PROJECT ROOT, because every skill script expects that.
root <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "..", ".."))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
```

```{r helpers, include = FALSE}
UC   <- "usecases/01_breathomics_biologics"
CFG  <- file.path(UC, "study_config.json")
RES  <- file.path(UC, "results")
rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") "Rscript.exe" else "Rscript")

## Run one skill script as a separate R process (exactly what Claude / MCP
## run_skill_script does). Skips the run if `done` exists, unless rerun = TRUE.
skill <- function(script, args = character(), done = NULL, show = 25) {
  cmd <- paste("Rscript", script, paste(args, collapse = " "))
  if (!is.null(done) && file.exists(done) && !isTRUE(params$rerun)) {
    cat("[cached] ", cmd, "\n", sep = ""); return(invisible())
  }
  out <- suppressWarnings(system2(rscript, shQuote(c(script, args)), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE))
  st <- attr(out, "status")
  cat("$ ", cmd, "\n", paste(utils::tail(out, show), collapse = "\n"), "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(st) && st != 0) stop("Step failed: ", cmd)
  invisible(out)
}
K <- ".claude/skills"
rd <- function(...) utils::read.csv(file.path(RES, ...), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
kt <- function(d, ...) knitr::kable(d, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, ...)
```

# What this notebook is

This is a **worked use case** for the 3TR DMP Analytical Engine. It walks
through the full analysis in

> Vassileva SM, Shahbazi Khamas S, *et al.* The impact of benralizumab and
> dupilumab on exhaled volatile organic compound profiles of severe asthma
> patients – a preliminary analysis. *Respiratory Medicine* 262 (2026) 109067.
> doi:10.1016/j.rmed.2026.109067

and runs each step with the engine's **skills** (R scripts under
`.claude/skills/`). The same steps can be run one by one through the MCP
server or by asking Claude.

**The data are synthetic.** The 3TR-ABC breath data are available only on
request, so `data/simulate_breath_data.R` generates a cohort with the same
design and with known ("planted") effects. Numbers below describe the
simulation, not the 3TR-ABC cohort. The point is the *workflow*: how to
reproduce the methods, what the outputs look like, and how to check them.

| Paper section | Engine skill | Section here |
|---|---|---|
| 2.1–2.2 design, clinical data | `prep-study-setup` | 2–3 |
| Table 1 | `stats-clinical-association --mode=table1` | 4 |
| 3.3, Table 3, Fig. 2 | `stats-clinical-association --mode=change` | 5 |
| 2.5 XCMS table, contaminants, log, batch (limma), Suppl. Fig. 1 | `prep-breathomics-gcms` *(new)* | 6 |
| 2.5 multilevel sPLS-DA, stepwise elimination, AUROC, LOSO-CV; Fig. 3, Table 2 | `ml-multilevel-splsda` *(new)* | 7 |
| Fig. 4 longitudinal boxplots | `ml-multilevel-splsda` panel boxplots | 7–8 |
| Table 4 Kendall correlations | `stats-clinical-association --mode=correlation` *(new)* | 9 |
| 3.6 medication (Mann–Whitney) | `stats-clinical-association --mode=exposure` *(new)* | 10 |
| VOC change by biologic | `stats-group-testing --design=between --change_from` | 11 |
| *(added)* all visits, missing M1 kept | `stats-mixed-models` *(new)*: `y ~ visit × biologic + (1 \| patient)` | 12 |

# Synthetic cohort

```{r simulate}
if (!file.exists(file.path(UC, "data", "metadata.csv")) || isTRUE(params$rerun)) {
  skill(file.path(UC, "data", "simulate_breath_data.R"), c(file.path(UC, "data"), params$seed))
}
meta  <- utils::read.csv(file.path(UC, "data", "metadata.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
truth <- utils::read.csv(file.path(UC, "data", "planted_truth.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
addmargins(table(biologic = meta$biologic, visit = factor(meta$visit, c("BL", "M1", "M4"))))
```

The generator mirrors the paper's design. It has 25 patients from two sites;
20 started dupilumab and 5 benralizumab. Breath was sampled at baseline (BL)
and 4 months (M4) for everyone, and at 1 month (M1) for 15 patients. Each
sample has 4,270 GC-MS ion fragments, of which 1,062 are known contaminants,
and samples were run in four GC-MS batches. These effects are planted:

```{r truth}
kt(head(truth[truth$type != "time_effect_background", ], 7))
```

Fifteen weaker, unnamed time-responsive fragments are also planted. Every
planted VOC responds in about 80% of patients; the rest is noise. The
two baseline traits are constant within each patient. The multilevel model
cannot see them, but the baseline correlations should.

Clinical response at 4 months, as defined in the paper:

```{r responders}
w <- reshape(meta[meta$visit %in% c("BL", "M4"), c("subject_id", "visit", "acq5", "fev1_pp")],
             idvar = "subject_id", timevar = "visit", direction = "wide")

  criterion = c("ACQ decrease >= 0.5", "ACQ < 1.5 at 4 months", "FEV1 improvement >= 10 % points"),
  n = c(sum(w$acq5.BL - w$acq5.M4 >= 0.5), sum(w$acq5.M4 < 1.5), sum(w$fev1_pp.M4 - w$fev1_pp.BL >= 10)),
  paper = c(22, 15, 10))
```

The paper's "≥10%" FEV1 improvement could mean percentage points or a
relative change; percentage points are used here.

# GC-MS preprocessing (Methods 2.5, Suppl. Fig. 1)

The paper's processing order is: XCMS → contaminant removal → log transform →
z-score → PCA to check batch → `limma` batch correction. The engine starts
from the aligned XCMS table, because raw chromatograms are not part of the
data contract.

```{r preprocess}
skill(file.path(K, "prep-breathomics-gcms/scripts/breath_preprocess.R"),
      c(paste0("--config=", CFG), "--layer=breath_voc"),
      done = file.path(RES, "data/breath_voc_processed_se.rds"), show = 0)
cat(readLines(file.path(RES, "qc/breath_voc_breath_qc.txt")), sep = "\n")
```

```{r suppfig1, out.width = "95%", echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root, RES, "qc/breath_voc_breath_pca.png"), rel_path = FALSE)
```

As in the paper, 4,270 fragments go in and 3,208 remain after contaminant
removal. Batch correction removes the batch structure from the leading PCs.
Here batches are nested within site, so the correction also removes site
differences; the QC file flags this.

# Multilevel sPLS-DA: baseline vs 4 months (Fig. 3, Table 2)

The paper's model, with its settings:

* fragments z-scored, **multilevel** decomposition (within-patient variation only);
* sPLS-DA with keepX tuned, then **stepwise backward elimination**: a feature is
  kept only if removing it drops the AUC by more than 5%, with a target AUC of about 0.9;
* AUROC of the final model on the full data, then **leave-one-subject-out CV**
  with the panel fixed.

The skill also adds a **nested cross-validation**, which repeats tuning and
elimination inside every outer fold (patient-grouped 5-fold × 5 repeats), and
a **within-patient permutation null**. These are the checks the paper's
design needs.

```{r splsda}
run <- "splsda/BLvsM4_breath_voc"
skill(file.path(K, "ml-multilevel-splsda/scripts/multilevel_splsda.R"),
      c(paste0("--config=", CFG), "--layer=breath_voc", "--visits=BL,M4",
        "--drop_max=0.05", "--target_auc=0.9", "--elim_auc=train",
        paste0("--n_perm=", params$n_perm), "--plot_visits=BL,M1,M4", "--colour_by=biologic"),
      done = file.path(RES, run, "performance.csv"), show = 0)
tun <- rd(run, "tuning.csv"); el <- rd(run, "elimination_log.csv")
cat(sprintf("Tuned keepX per component: %s; %d fragments entered elimination; final panel: %d\n",
            paste(tun$keepX[tapply(seq_len(nrow(tun)), tun$comp, function(i) i[which.max(tun$loso_auc[i])])], collapse = ", "),
            el$n_features[1], utils::tail(el$n_features, 1)))
kt(utils::tail(el, 8))
```

**Table 2 equivalent: the selected panel**

```{r panel}
panel <- rd(run, "panel.csv")
panel$planted <- ifelse(panel$feature %in% truth$feature[truth$type == "time_effect"], "planted VOC",
                 ifelse(panel$feature %in% truth$feature, "planted background", "noise"))
kt(panel[, c("feature", "compound", "mz", "rt_s", "class", "formula", "direction", "n_up", "n_down", "planted")])
```

```{r fig3, fig.show = "hold", out.width = "48%", echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root, RES, run, c("sample_plot.png", "roc.png")), rel_path = FALSE)
```

**Performance: four estimates**

```{r performance}
perf <- rd(run, "performance.csv")
kt(perf[, c("estimate", "auc", "auc_ci_low", "auc_ci_high", "paired_acc", "perm_null_mean_auc", "perm_p_auc")])
perm <- rd(run, "permutation.csv")
summary(perm[, c("n_features", "auc_train", "auc_loso_fixed_panel", "paired_acc_loso_fixed_panel")])
```

How to read this:

* **A (training)** and **B (LOSO, panel fixed)** are the two estimates the
  paper reports (0.89 and 0.78 there). The panel was chosen on the same 25
  patients for both, so neither is an independent estimate.
* The **permutation null** reruns the same pipeline after flipping BL/M4
  labels within random patients, so there is *no* treatment effect. It
  still gives training AUCs around `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(perm$auc_train))` and LOSO
  AUCs around `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(perm$auc_loso_fixed_panel))`. The observed
  training AUC sits at permutation *p* = `r sprintf("%.2f", perf$perm_p_auc[1])` (`r nrow(perm)` permutations).
  With about 3,000
  fragments, about 25 pairs and within-patient centring, high A and B values
  are expected **even without a real effect**. An A or B value alone
  therefore cannot show that VOCs changed.
* **C (nested CV)** is the honest estimate. Use paired accuracy (the share of
  patients whose 4-month sample scores higher than their baseline sample),
  not pooled AUC: each fold's model puts scores on its own scale. The table
  gives the mean over 5 repeats, with the min–max range in the CI columns.
  Nested *leave-one-subject-out* is available (`--nested_folds=loso`) but
  is biased downwards when selection is this aggressive (see the skill's SKILL.md).

Per-repeat nested results, and how often each panel feature was selected
again across the 25 nested fold fits:

```{r stability}
kt(rd(run, "nested_repeats.csv"))
np <- rd(run, "nested_panels.csv")
fr <- table(unlist(strsplit(np$features, ";")))
data.frame(feature = panel$feature, compound = panel$compound,
           fold_fits_selected = as.integer(ifelse(is.na(fr[panel$feature]), 0, fr[panel$feature])), of = nrow(np))
kt(as.data.frame(sort(fr, decreasing = TRUE)[1:8], responseName = "fold_fits"), col.names = c("feature (top 8 across nested fits)", "fold fits"))
```

**Recall of the planted truth.** The tuned sPLS-DA model, before
elimination, contained
`r sum(truth$feature[truth$type == "time_effect"] %in% el$removed | truth$feature[truth$type == "time_effect"] %in% panel$feature)`
of the 5 planted VOCs. The elimination rule then cut it down to the smallest
set that keeps the training AUC ≥ 0.9.

# The published 5-VOC panel as a fixed panel (Fig. 4)

To mirror the paper's figures for the five compounds it reports, we evaluate
that panel directly, with no selection (`--panel`). In the simulation these
are the planted VOCs.

```{r paper-panel}
v5 <- truth$feature[truth$type == "time_effect"]
run5 <- "splsda/BLvsM4_breath_voc_paper5"
skill(file.path(K, "ml-multilevel-splsda/scripts/multilevel_splsda.R"),
      c(paste0("--config=", CFG), "--layer=breath_voc", "--visits=BL,M4",
        paste0("--panel=", paste(v5, collapse = ",")), "--plot_visits=BL,M1,M4",
        "--colour_by=biologic", "--tag=paper5"),
      done = file.path(RES, run5, "performance.csv"), show = 0)
kt(rd(run5, "performance.csv")[1:2, c("estimate", "auc", "auc_ci_low", "auc_ci_high", "paired_acc")])
kt(rd(run5, "panel.csv")[, c("compound", "class", "loading_comp1", "mean_change_z", "direction", "n_up", "n_down")])
```

```{r fig4, out.width = "100%", echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root, RES, run5, "panel_boxplots.png"), rel_path = FALSE)
```

Lines connect each patient's visits and are coloured by biologic. As
planted, methyl isobutyl ketone and the alkanes/ether decrease, and
2-ethyl-1-hexanol increases.

# Baseline VOC–clinical correlations (Table 4)

```{r kendall}
skill(file.path(K, "stats-clinical-association/scripts/clinical_association.R"),
      c(paste0("--config=", CFG), "--mode=correlation", "--layer=breath_voc",
        paste0("--features=", paste(v5, collapse = ",")), "--vars=acq5,blood_eos,ige,feno,fev1_pp",
        "--visit=BL", paste0("--boot=", params$boot), "--tag=BL_paper5"),
      done = file.path(RES, "clinical/correlation_BL_paper5/kendall.csv"), show = 0)
kt(rd("clinical/correlation_BL_paper5/kendall_table.csv"))
kd <- rd("clinical/correlation_BL_paper5/kendall.csv")
kt(kd[kd$p_value < 0.05, c("label", "clinical", "n", "tau", "z", "p_value", "tau_ci_low", "tau_ci_high")])
```

The two planted baseline traits are recovered: 2-ethyl-1-hexanol with ACQ
(positive) and 1,1′-oxybis(decane) with blood eosinophils (negative). There
are 25 unadjusted tests here, so about one would fall below *p* < 0.05 by
chance; any extra "hits" in the table should be read that way. After BH
adjustment:

```{r kendall-bh}
kd$p_BH <- p.adjust(kd$p_value, "BH")
kt(kd[order(kd$p_BH)[1:4], c("label", "clinical", "tau", "p_value", "p_BH")])
```

# Influence of medication (Section 3.6)

```{r exposure}
skill(file.path(K, "stats-clinical-association/scripts/clinical_association.R"),
      c(paste0("--config=", CFG), "--mode=exposure", "--layer=breath_voc",
        paste0("--features=", paste(v5, collapse = ",")),
        "--exposures=ocs_maintenance,lama,ltra,ics_dose", "--visit=BL", "--tag=BL_paper5"),
      done = file.path(RES, "clinical/exposure_BL_paper5/exposure_tests.csv"), show = 0)
ex <- rd("clinical/exposure_BL_paper5/exposure_tests.csv")
kt(ex[order(ex$p_value)[1:6], c("exposure", "label", "groups", "test", "p_value")])
```

No medication was planted in the simulation, so any small *p*-values here
are chance. With only 4 patients on maintenance OCS, this test has almost no power.

# VOC change by biologic

The paper saw no visual difference in VOC trajectories between biologics.
The engine's existing `stats-group-testing` skill tests that directly. It
compares the change from baseline (M4 − BL) between dupilumab (n = 20) and
benralizumab (n = 5) for every fragment, with FDR correction.

```{r by-biologic}
skill(file.path(K, "stats-group-testing/scripts/group_tests.R"),
      c(paste0("--config=", CFG), "--design=between", "--by=group", "--visit=M4",
        "--change_from=BL", "--layers=breath_voc"),
      done = file.path(RES, "tests/between_group_M4_minusBL/breath_voc_tests.csv"), show = 0)
bt <- rd("tests/between_group_M4_minusBL/breath_voc_tests.csv")
cat(sprintf("%d fragments; min FDR (Wilcoxon) = %.2f\n", nrow(bt), min(bt$fdr_wilcox, na.rm = TRUE)))
kt(bt[bt$feature %in% v5, intersect(c("feature", "comparison", "mean_diff", "cohens_d", "p_wilcox", "fdr_wilcox"), names(bt))])
```

With 5 benralizumab patients, only very large between-drug differences could
be detected. "No difference" here means "not detectable", not "the same".

# Mixed-effects models using all three visits (added)

The paper's tests use only the patients with both baseline and 4-month
samples, and the 1-month visit enters only the plots. A **linear mixed
model** uses every available sample, keeping the 10 patients without a
1-month breath sample. It also models within-patient correlation with a
random intercept:

`y ~ visit × biologic + (1 | patient)`

Here `visit` is a factor (BL, M1, M4), so no shape is assumed. The time effect, the
time × biologic interaction and the time effect within each biologic are
likelihood-ratio tests. Changes versus baseline come from `emmeans`. The
skill is `stats-mixed-models`.

## Clinical trajectories

```{r lmm-clinical}
skill(file.path(K, "stats-mixed-models/scripts/mixed_models.R"),
      c(paste0("--config=", CFG), "--mode=clinical", "--vars=blood_eos,feno,ige,fev1_pp,acq5,aqlq",
        "--log=blood_eos,feno,ige", "--by=group"),
      done = file.path(RES, "mixed/clinical_factor_bygroup_intercept/lmm_results.csv"), show = 0)
lc <- rd("mixed/clinical_factor_bygroup_intercept/lmm_results.csv")
kt(lc[, c("label", "n_obs", "n_subjects", "p_time", "fdr_time", "p_interaction", "fdr_interaction",
          "p_time_benralizumab", "p_time_dupilumab", "icc")])
cc <- rd("mixed/clinical_factor_bygroup_intercept/contrasts.csv")
kt(cc[cc$variable %in% c("blood_eos", "feno"), c("label", "contrast", ".grp", "estimate", "lower.CL", "upper.CL", "p.value")])
```

```{r lmm-clinical-fig, out.width = "100%", echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root, RES, "mixed/clinical_factor_bygroup_intercept/trajectories.png"), rel_path = FALSE)
```

The models show what Table 3 hides by pooling both drugs. Eosinophils
**rise transiently on dupilumab (largest at 1 month) and collapse on benralizumab**: the interaction is the
strongest effect in the table. FeNO and IgE fall mainly on dupilumab. On the
log scale, contrasts are differences in log units, so exp(estimate) is the
ratio to baseline. ACQ and AQLQ were not collected at 1 month, so they
contribute only BL and M4.

## VOCs: every fragment, all visits

```{r lmm-voc}
skill(file.path(K, "stats-mixed-models/scripts/mixed_models.R"),
      c(paste0("--config=", CFG), "--mode=features", "--layer=breath_voc", "--by=group", "--report_top=12"),
      done = file.path(RES, "mixed/features_breath_voc_factor_bygroup_intercept/lmm_results.csv"), show = 0)
lv <- rd("mixed/features_breath_voc_factor_bygroup_intercept/lmm_results.csv")
lv$planted <- ifelse(lv$variable %in% v5, "planted VOC", ifelse(lv$variable %in% truth$feature, "planted background", ""))
cat(sprintf("%d fragments; time effect FDR < 0.05: %d; time x biologic FDR < 0.05: %d\n",
            nrow(lv), sum(lv$fdr_time < 0.05), sum(lv$fdr_interaction < 0.05)))
kt(head(lv[, c("variable", "label", "p_time", "fdr_time", "p_interaction", "fdr_interaction", "icc", "planted")], 12))
cat("Rank of the planted VOCs by time-effect p:", paste(sprintf("%s %d", lv$label[lv$planted == "planted VOC"],
    which(lv$planted == "planted VOC")), collapse = "; "), "\n")
```

```{r lmm-voc-fig, out.width = "100%", echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root, RES, "mixed/features_breath_voc_factor_bygroup_intercept/trajectories.png"), rel_path = FALSE)
```

```{r lmm-voc-int}
kt(lv[lv$fdr_interaction < 0.05, c("variable", "label", "p_interaction", "fdr_interaction",
                                    "p_time_benralizumab", "p_time_dupilumab", "planted")])
```

How the two approaches compare:

* The mixed model tests **each fragment** with FDR control across all
  3,208. sPLS-DA instead selects a *combination*, which gives no per-VOC
  error control. The two answer different questions, so report both.
* Four of the five planted VOCs rank in the top five by time effect.
  2-ethyl-1-hexanol ranks lower in this simulation (see the printed ranks).
  At n = 25 only the two strongest pass FDR < 0.05; the others are best
  described as "top-ranked, not significant after correction".
* The interaction hits above are *not* planted, so they are false
  positives. The likely cause is that, with only 5 benralizumab patients,
  one or two extreme patients can produce a "drug-specific" trajectory.
  Treat any VOC × biologic finding as exploratory until there are more
  benralizumab patients.

# Replication scorecard

```{r scorecard, echo = FALSE}
p5 <- rd(run5, "performance.csv")
data.frame(
  item = c("Fragments after contaminant removal", "VOCs in final sPLS-DA panel",
           "Training AUROC (95% CI)", "LOSO AUROC, fixed panel (95% CI)", "Nested CV paired accuracy, mean (range)",
           "Permutation-null training AUROC (mean)",
           "Published 5 VOCs: training / LOSO AUROC",
           "2-ethyl-1-hexanol ~ ACQ (tau, p)", "1,1'-oxybis(decane) ~ eosinophils (tau, p)"),
  paper = c("3208", "5", "0.89 (0.79-0.99)", "0.78 (0.65-0.91)", "not done", "not done",
            "0.89 / 0.78", "0.40, 0.008", "-0.30, 0.035"),
  this_run = c(
    sub(".*-> (\\d+) fragments.*", "\\1", grep("Known contaminants", readLines(file.path(RES, "qc/breath_voc_breath_qc.txt")), value = TRUE)),
    nrow(panel),
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", perf$auc[1], perf$auc_ci_low[1], perf$auc_ci_high[1]),
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", perf$auc[2], perf$auc_ci_low[2], perf$auc_ci_high[2]),
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", perf$paired_acc[3], perf$paired_acc_ci_low[3], perf$paired_acc_ci_high[3]),
    sprintf("%.2f", mean(perm$auc_train)),
    sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", p5$auc[1], p5$auc[2]),
    with(kd[kd$label == "2-ethyl-1-hexanol" & kd$clinical == "acq5", ], sprintf("%.2f, %.3g", tau, p_value)),
    with(kd[kd$label == "1,1'-oxybis(decane)" & kd$clinical == "blood_eos", ], sprintf("%.2f, %.3g", tau, p_value))))
```

Every "this run" number comes from the synthetic data and will change with
the seed. Only the paper column refers to the real cohort.

# What the replication shows

1. **The workflow reproduces end to end with engine skills.** Three methods
   were missing and are now skills: breath GC-MS preprocessing, multilevel
   sPLS-DA with backward elimination and LOSO, and the Kendall / Mann–Whitney
   / paired-change clinical statistics. A fourth, mixed-effects models, was
   added to use all three visits.
2. **Mixed models add what the paired design throws away.** They keep the 1-month
   visit and patients with missing samples, and they test drug × time
   directly. The eosinophil response to the two biologics is opposite, and
   pooled paired tests average it away.
3. **The published validation is optimistic by design.** Features were selected
   once on all patients (stated in the paper), so the LOSO-CV of the fixed
   panel is not independent. The permutation null shows the pipeline can
   score highly with no effect. The nested estimate and the re-selection
   frequencies are the numbers to carry forward to the full 3TR-ABC cohort.
4. **The elimination rule is unstable.** "Remove while the AUC drops ≤ 5%"
   evaluated on the training AUC tends towards one or two features, and which
   features survive depends on chance. Inside the nested folds it often
   leaves a single VOC. The skill offers `--elim_auc=loso` and
   `--target_auc=NA` for sensitivity analyses.
5. **Ambiguities in the paper's methods,** with the choices made here (all
   are skill options):
   relative vs absolute 5% AUC drop (relative);
   AUC for elimination (training);
   number of sPLS-DA components (2);
   how keepX was tuned (sequential LOSO AUC);
   CI method for Kendall's tau (bootstrap);
   the log base and how zeros were handled (log2, half-minimum);
   the definition of FEV1 ≥ 10% (percentage points).

## Methods paragraph (template)

> Exhaled-breath GC-MS feature tables were processed with the DMP-AE
> `prep-breathomics-gcms` skill: known contaminants were removed, intensities were
> log2-transformed (zeros set to half the fragment minimum) and batch effects
> were removed with `limma::removeBatchEffect`, preserving visit. Fragments
> were z-scored, and within-patient variation was isolated by multilevel
> decomposition. Sparse PLS-DA (2 components; keepX tuned by leave-one-subject-out AUC)
> was followed by backward elimination (`ml-multilevel-splsda`; engine:
> `r sub(".*engine: (\\w+).*", "\\1", readLines(file.path(RES, run, "summary.txt"))[2])`).
> Performance was estimated by patient-grouped 5-fold cross-validation
> (5 repeats), with keepX tuning and elimination repeated inside each
> training fold (nested). Significance was
> assessed against `r params$n_perm` within-patient label permutations.
> Clinical changes were tested with paired t or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests
> according to the Shapiro–Wilk test, and baseline associations with Kendall's
> tau (`stats-clinical-association`). Longitudinal changes over all three
> visits were modelled with linear mixed models (visit × biologic fixed
> effects, random patient intercept; likelihood-ratio tests, BH-FDR across
> fragments; `stats-mixed-models`).
